subject.title: [Feature]: Expose before_tool_call/after_tool_call in internal hooks system

question: Should managed HOOK.md hooks be allowed to block or rewrite tool calls, or should enforceable tool-call policy remain typed-plugin-only with clearer validation for unsupported HOOK.md event names?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing pre-tool execution to managed hooks changes OpenClaw's security and plugin API boundary; automation cannot choose trust, ordering, timeout, failure, and compatibility semantics safely.

options.title: Design managed tool-call hooks
options.body: Add a typed managed/internal before and after tool-call API that composes with plugin hooks, trusted policies, and all tool execution surfaces, with focused tests and public docs.

options.title: Keep plugin-only policy
options.body: Reject or warn on before_tool_call and after_tool_call in HOOK.md metadata, and point users to typed plugin hooks or ClawHub-packaged code plugins for enforceable tool policy.

options.title: Expose telemetry only
options.body: Expose non-blocking after-call or observation-only events to managed hooks while keeping pre-tool blocking and parameter rewrites in the typed plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Design managed tool-call hooks
recommendation.body: Add a typed managed/internal before and after tool-call API that composes with plugin hooks, trusted policies, and all tool execution surfaces, with focused tests and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the original internal hook surface and already provided maintainer signal on this canonical tracker.
